newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel approves West Bank settlement expansion.
newsitem.headline: Israel approves West Bank settlement expansion.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai has approved plans for a huge expansion of a Jewish settlement in the occupied West Bank, an official said on Monday.
The Palestinian Authority immediately condemned the approval as a link in the policies of the Israeli government to wreck the peace process and return to an atmosphere of war.

The plans call for the construction of 1,200 new homes, a country club, a senior citizens' home, a field school and a study centre for ultra-orthodox Jews in Emmanuel settlement, near the Palestinian-ruled city of Nablus.
"We have finally received all the permits," said Emmanuel local council head Shmuel Lanza when asked about reports that Mordechai had approved the plan.

Mordechai must give final approval to any expansion of Jewish settlements in the West Bank, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war. The Defence Ministry declined comment on the Emmanuel plans.
"According to plans, we will begin building in January," Lanza told Reuters, saying 500 homes would be built in the project's first phase.

The "Emmanuel 2000" campaign will be one the largest building projects for Jews in the West Bank since right-wing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu overturned a four-year freeze on settlement construction after taking power in June.

Israeli media reports said in August that Mordechai had approved construction of between 2,000 and 3,500 housing units in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, where some 130,000 Jews have settled amongst more than two million Arabs since 1967.
Palestinians view the settlers as a provocation and vehemently oppose any expansion of the Jewish presence in territories where they hope to build an independent state.
The Palestinian Authority blasted the Emmanuel project.

"It is a link in the chain of policies which this government has pursued since it assumed power in Israel to torpedo the peace process and to return to an atmosphere of conflict and war in the region," the Palestinian Information Ministry said in a statement.
Lanza said Emmanuel lay in a "security belt" of West Bank settlements which he said would be annexed to the Jewish state after a final peace deal was reached with the Palestinians.
"To the best of my understanding, this will certainly be part of the land of Israel at the end of this process," he said.
Under a 1993 Israel-PLO peace deal, the fate of Jewish settlements will be determined in talks on a final peace accord to be completed by 1999.

Israel's Globes financial newspaper said the $37 million project would be funded primarily by private developers. Lanza said some government funds would be used but did not elaborate. Israel's housing ministry said it had no connection to the project, a spokesman said.
Mossi Raz, secretary-general of Israel's strongly anti-settlement Peace Now group, condemned the plan, saying it could spark violent Palestinian protests.

"The government is playing with fire. I don't know what will be the next spark, when the next tunnel will come," Raz said, referring to an archaeological tunnel in Arab East Jerusalem which Netanyahu opened in September, igniting fierce clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops.
